deep.reconstruction:
Context: E260 builds a one-dimensional model of steady efflux through a chain of tubes (reservoir of cross-section ff, tubes gg, hh, ii, orifice kk). Wall friction is a loss proportional to (length/width) times kinetic head, which gives exponential factors 𝔄 = e^{-αa/f}, etc. Here v is the 'altitude due to the velocity' at the orifice, i.e. u²/2g, not the velocity itself. In §40 Euler sets α = 0 and gets v = q·f⁴/(f⁴−k⁴), where q = AI is the total head. This is Bernoulli's equation with the velocity-of-approach correction: u²/2g = q/(1−(A_k/A_f)²).

This page interprets that formula.

§41: If ff is not much larger than kk, then v > q. The jet leaves faster than Torricelli's value √(2gq), which 'will seem no small paradox'. Euler resolves it from his hypothesis. The upper vessel is kept full by water that is assumed to arrive already moving with the surface's descent speed. That water does not start its fall from rest, so it gains more than the head q. In energy terms, kinetic energy is supplied at the inflow.

§42: For kk = ff the frictionless formula gives v = ∞. Euler reads this as the absence of any steady state. With inflow equal to outflow at the same speed, the column accelerates continually, like a freely falling body. For kk > ff a steady state is even less possible, and in addition the water separates from the tube walls.

§43: Methodological conclusion. The theory applies only if water is poured in at exactly the surface's subsidence speed. To compare with experiments, take a very large reservoir so that k⁴/f⁴ (written 𝔣) can be neglected. Slow pouring then does not disturb the motion. The next page quantifies this: f > 3k gives 𝔣 < 1/81.
errors: No mathematical error on this page.

Implicit caveat not stated by Euler: the infinite v for kk = ff is a frictionless artefact. In his own general formula (§39) with α > 0, the denominator 1 − 𝔅ℭ𝔇𝔣 − αB…, evaluated at 𝔣 = 1, stays positive. Friction would therefore give a finite 'terminal' steady flow. His free-fall analogy holds only for α = 0.
Strictly, the physical effect of kk > ff (jet separation) lies outside the one-dimensional model; Euler mentions it only qualitatively.

ideas.what: Efflux head with finite reservoir: v = q·f⁴/(f⁴−k⁴), exceeding the Torricelli head when areas are comparable
ideas.where_published: E260 and Euler's earlier/later hydraulic papers (e.g. on efflux and pipe flow)

ideas.what: Resolution of the paradox: the inflow brings kinetic energy, so the water's fall does not start from rest
ideas.modern_name: Energy balance with inlet kinetic head

ideas.what: Singular case kk = ff: no steady state, unbounded acceleration like free fall; kk > ff causes separation from the walls
ideas.modern_name: Non-existence of steady inviscid flow; flow separation

ideas.what: Experimental design: large reservoir so k⁴/f⁴ is negligible

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard velocity-of-approach discussion with a sensible physical interpretation, known since Bernoulli's Hydrodynamica. Nothing here seems absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Transcription is essentially faithful to the image; the long s is rendered as 's' on this page but as 'ſ' on the neighbouring pages (cosmetic only).
